title: Stride-aware reservation protocol and sparse reuse orchestrator
creator: Asha Raman
description: Problem: For mixed workloads with interleaved short and long contexts, our paged KV cache sees a pattern of sparse hot entries (widely separated token spans) that cause fragmentation and frequent small prefetches. This increases decode tail latency and amplifies kernel selection oscillation on heterogeneous HW. Goal: design a stride-aware reservation protocol plus a sparse-reuse orchestrator that reduces fragmentation, improves decode SLOs for long-tail requests, and stabilizes kernel affinity decisions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end 99th percentile decode latency reduced by >=10% on mixed workload benchmark. 2) KV reservation hit-rate improvement >=15% for sparse long-context traces. 3) No >5% regression in median latency or throughput on short-sequence microbenchmarks. 4) Automated simulation harness and dashboard for rollout gating.
proposal_summary: 1) Reservation protocol: allocate ephemeral stride reservations instead of contiguous pages for predicted sparse spans; reservations are lightweight metadata entries that reserve decode admission tokens and kernel affinity. 2) Sparse reuse orchestrator: candidate selection that coalesces non-contiguous spans into a compact reuse set using a locality heuristic (stride distance, recency, and predicted decode continuation). 3) Kernel affinity stabilization: use reservation signals to bias the kernel selector and avoid rapid switches when a request is likely to touch reserved sparse spans. 4) Admission & eviction policy: reservations have decaying soft timers and can be promoted to full residency on repeated hits or immediate prefetch if decode window predicts imminent use.
design_notes:
- Trade-offs: reservations reduce overhead of full page allocations but add metadata churn; need fast path for eviction.
- Heuristic tuning: combine stride distance, token-visit frequency, and request-level TTL to score candidates.
- Backpressure: when reservation saturation is high, fall back to adaptive coalescing (merge small reservations into a temporary contiguous prefetch).
- Safety: reservations are tenant-scoped to avoid cross-tenant resource starvation.
- Metrics: reservation_count, reservation_hits, promotion_rate, reservation_latency, kernel_switch_rate.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement simulation-only reservation metadata and orchestrator in bench harness, run offline traces to tune scoring. Phase 2 (runtime prototype): add reservation fast-path in KV allocator and a kernel-affinity hint channel. Phase 3 (canary): deploy to runtime-1.22 canary ring with opt-in flag; collect metrics and evaluate against acceptance criteria. Phase 4: rollout with auto-tuning and console telemetry.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: extra metadata overhead increases GC pressure. Mitigate by compacting reservation records and using generational TTLs.
- Risk: wrong promotions cause wasted prefetch/latency spikes. Mitigate with conservative promotion thresholds and canary tuning.
- Risk: kernel selector bias reduces throughput on other tenants. Mitigate by bounding affinity weight and dynamically decaying hints.
